name: New Haven telephone exchange
summary: In January 1878 Coy's switchboard in New Haven began connecting paying telephone subscribers to one another, in what the National Park Service describes as the first commercial telephone exchange.
description: Coy switchboard and New Haven District Telephone Company subscriber exchange in a Boardman Building storefront.
tier_reason: Retain1 for an exchange architecture/service; the missing telephone invention does not make the existing exchange a wrong historical object. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

impact.note: One town's exchange, giving its subscribers switched calls for the first time, soon copied elsewhere as similar exchanges opened; implies tier 2, below reviewed tier 1.

market.note: The cited source documents a paid public service or commercial product release; it does not establish the first possible sale or offer.

evidence.supports: The NPS account dates commercial operation to 28 January and reports 21 initial subscribers.

evidence.locator: Section VI, paragraph beginning Mr. Coy commenced installing
evidence.supports: The 1907 account reports first service on 21 January to about 30 subscribers and formal opening on 28 January.

date.label: by 1878-01-28
date.basis: The 1907 account dates initial service to 21 January and formal opening to 28 January; the NPS describes service beginning on 28 January. Earliest availability is unresolved.

events.statement: Coy’s New Haven exchange was providing subscriber service by 28 January 1878; the 1907 account reports earlier service on 21 January.
events.caveats: Accounts differ on the first service date and subscriber count: NPS reports 21 subscribers with the 28 January start, while De Land reports approximately 30 for initial service on 21 January and a 28 January formal opening. The record establishes availability by 28 January, not an undisputed first day or headcount.

events.statement: The New Haven exchange advertised an annual telephone rental for offices and homes.
events.caveats: The price does not establish actual household affordability; the retrospective reports shared lines.

evidence.locator: Section VI, rates and February 1878 advertising
evidence.supports: Reports the $18 annual rate for office or home telephones and its February advertising.

date.basis: The retrospective discusses the night operator and pay during early 1878; the precise payroll period is not stated.

events.statement: The retrospective reports the monthly pay and hours of a night operator at the early New Haven exchange.
events.caveats: The exact period and whether pay was typical for other staff are unspecified.

evidence.supports: Reports a night operator’s monthly salary and hours.

date.label: 21 February 1878
date.basis: The date is printed on the New Haven District Telephone Company broadside.

events.statement: The New Haven District Telephone Company listed subscribers by name and gave the opening hours of its 219 Chapel Street office.
events.caveats: The listing includes organizations and names repeated for different premises. It gives no connection or billing status for individual listings. The prospect of all-night opening after 1 March is announced in the footer.

evidence.locator: Single sheet, heading, both listing columns and office-hours footer
evidence.supports: The dated broadside identifies the publisher and office, enumerates listed names or locations and gives hours of 6 a.m. to 2 a.m.

The record establishes availability by 28 January, not an undisputed first day or headcount. This is the earliest supported record currently established here, not certification of absolute priority.

research.note: Proposed distinct configuration and community entry; requires independent review. Independent reader checked the two early opening accounts and both source-scoped price and pay measures. The differing launch counts remain unresolved; affordability is not established. The 21 February broadside adds source-scoped listing counts and stated hours.

measures.subject: New Haven office or house telephone subscription

evidence.supports: Reports $18 annually for office or house telephone.

measures.conditions: Shared single-wire circuits typically served 10–16 subscribers; price does not establish whether a household could afford it.

measures.subject: New Haven exchange night operator

evidence.supports: Reports $15 per month and a 5 p.m.–8 a.m. shift.

measures.conditions: Specific night-operator role; shift reported as 5 p.m. to 8 a.m.; not a general wage or disposable-income estimate.

measures.subject: February subscriber sheet
measures.method: Count the 11 residence, 3 physician, 2 dentist, 8 miscellaneous, 20 store and factory, 4 market, and 2 stable rows. Include separate location rows printed with ditto marks.
measures.conditions: M. F. Tyler appears twice and New Haven Flour Co. occupies four rows. The tally gives the number of printed listings. Unique people, paying accounts, connected stations, lines and completed calls are unmeasured.

evidence.locator: Single sheet, all seven listing headings and their rows
evidence.supports: Visual row tally of the complete sheet.

measures.subject: February subscriber sheet
measures.method: Count each row after Residences up to the Physicians heading.
measures.conditions: The directory supplies names in this section. Household identity, occupancy, line status and an eligible household denominator are unknown.

evidence.locator: Single sheet, left column, Residences heading
evidence.supports: Eleven printed entries appear under Residences.
